blurb_html: Momofuku’s cold-sauce noodles, softened: half the ginger, more scallion, and hot oil to take off the burn.
description: Momofuku’s cold-sauce noodles, softened: half the ginger, more scallion, and hot oil to take off the burn.
equipment_html: Heatproof bowl (bigger than you think — the oil bubbles up)

items.amount_html: ¼ cup finely minced (about a 5 cm piece)

intro_html: Momofuku’s ginger scallion sauce is just scallions, ginger, oil and a little seasoning stirred together raw — and their amount of ginger is hot and hard on the palate. This version keeps the idea but makes it softer: half the ginger, a bit more scallion and oil, the oil poured over hot to mellow the raw ginger, and a pinch of sugar and a drop of sesame oil to round it off. Best with the baked-soda ramen noodles.

mise.items_html: soy · vinegar · sugar · sesame oil · salt
mise.name: Seasoning

notes.html:
• Momofuku’s original, stirred together raw:
    • 2½ cups sliced scallions
    • ½ cup minced ginger
    • ⅓ cup grapeseed oil
    • 1½ tsp usukuchi
    • ¾ tsp sherry vinegar
    • ¾ tsp kosher salt
  • This version:
    • ginger halved to ¼ cup, minced finer
    • scallions up to 3 cups
    • oil up to ½ cup, poured over hot
    • soy up to 2 tsp, salt down to ½ tsp
    • added: 1 tsp sugar and ½ tsp toasted sesame oil

• Cut the ginger to 2 tablespoons.
  • Blanch the minced ginger in boiling water for 30 seconds and drain it before the hot oil goes on.
  • Let the sauce sit an hour before using — it keeps mellowing.
  • Add more scallion rather than more seasoning.

• Momofuku serves these with quick pickles, pan-roasted cauliflower, bamboo shoots and nori.
  • The cucumber pickle works well as the pickle.
Adapted from Momofuku’s ginger scallion noodles (David Chang and Peter Meehan, Momofuku, 2009), made gentler and written in my own words.

steps.body_html:
• Slice the whites and light-green parts thinly (a little of the dark green is fine) — about 3 cups.
  • Put them in the heatproof bowl.

how.caption: Slice the scallions thinly — whites and light greens.

steps.title: Slice the scallions

steps.body_html:
• Peel with the edge of a spoon, slice thinly, cut into matchsticks, then mince finely — smaller bits bite less.
  • Measure ¼ cup, no more, and add it to the scallions.

images.alt: Mince the ginger — less than you think

how.caption: Mince the ginger finely — and use only ¼ cup.

steps.title: Mince the ginger — less than you think

steps.body_html:
• Heat the oil in a small saucepan until it shimmers (about 170 °C — a scallion slice dropped in sizzles hard).
  • Pour it over the scallions and ginger. It sizzles and bubbles up — this takes the raw burn off the ginger.
  • Stir once.

how.caption: Heat the oil until it shimmers, then pour it over — it sizzles and takes the edge off the ginger.

steps.title: Pour hot oil over

steps.body_html:
• Stir in:
    • light soy sauce (usukuchi) 2 tsp
    • sherry vinegar ¾ tsp
    • sugar 1 tsp
    • toasted sesame oil ½ tsp
    • salt ½ tsp
  • Leave it 15–20 minutes for the flavours to settle, then taste and adjust the salt.
  • It keeps 2 days in the fridge; stir before using.

how.caption: Stir in the soy, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and salt; rest 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Season and rest

steps.body_html: Boil the noodles (homemade: 1½–2 minutes; bought: as the packet says), drain well and shake off the water.
steps.title: Cook the noodles

steps.body_html:
• Toss each bowl of hot noodles with 5–6 tablespoons of sauce until every strand is coated.
  • Top with a couple of:
    • pickled cucumber a few slices
    • toasted nori 1 sheet
    • extra sliced scallion a pinch

how.caption: Toss the hot noodles with 5–6 tablespoons of sauce.

steps.title: Toss and top
